s0001.x: chào + the person you greet; em = you, for someone younger. Xin chào exists but is rare in casual speech: you greet the person by what you call them.

s0002.x: What a younger person says to you: you are anh, older brother. You hear this one; your own greeting is Chào em.

s0003.x: No verb 'to be' before an adjective: em khỏe = you (are) well. không at the end makes a yes-or-no question, like 嗎; in Saigon you often hear hông.

s0004.x: anh = I when you speak to someone younger. Còn + person = and what about…, like 那…呢.

s0005.x: To your father you are con (child) and he is ba. Dạ opens a polite answer to someone older.

s0006.x: Thanks usually names the person: cảm ơn em, cảm ơn anh, cảm ơn ba.

s0007.x: Literally 沒有什麼: the usual answer to thanks.

s0008.x: Literally 我名字是 Mike: the topic first, then là. là links two nouns, like 是.

s0009.x: Question words stand where the answer goes: Em tên gì? Anh tên (là) Mike. The question needs no là.

s0010.x: rất before an adjective = 很. được before a verb = get to (do): vui được gặp = glad to get to meet. A little textbook, fine in a first chat.

s0120.x: chưa at the end asks whether something has happened yet, 了嗎. A friendly greeting, like 吃飽沒.

s0121.x: rồi after the verb = already, 了. The answer to …chưa? is …rồi (yes) or chưa (not yet).

s0035.x: trời = sky, here the weather. quá after an adjective = so, really: 好涼喔.

s0036.x: Time words come first. trời mưa = the sky rains, 下雨.

s0037.x: muốn + verb = want to, 想. The order is the Mandarin one: 我想買咖啡.

s0038.x: Cho anh + thing = give me…, the standard way to order. ly is the classifier for a glass. What describes the noun follows it: cà phê sữa đá = coffee, (with) milk, (with) ice.

s0039.x: The same frame: number + classifier + noun, as in 一碗河粉.

s0040.x: chưa at the end: has it happened yet? Here: do you know yet, have you heard?

s0041.x: chưa before a verb = not yet, 還沒. The short answer simply repeats it.

s0042.x: Adjectives work like verbs, no 是 needed: anh mệt = I (am) tired.

s0066.x: ừ = the casual yes to a friend or someone younger. hiểu rồi = got it, 懂了.

s0067.x: về = go back (home, to where you belong). No word for 'to': về nhà = 回家.

s0068.x: nay after a time word = this: trưa nay, tối nay. The subject is dropped, as so often in Mandarin.

s0069.x: classifier + noun + này = this…: cái chai này = 這個瓶子. này comes after the noun.

s0070.x: thôi = stop, okay then, 算了 or 好了. đủ rồi = 夠了.

s0071.x: No classifier needed here: cà phê này = this coffee. ngon = tasty, for food and drinks.

s0072.x: người + place = the people from there. How you do something follows the verb: nói nhanh = 說得快.

s0073.x: chút = a bit, after the adjective: chậm chút = 慢一點. nha softens the request.

s0074.x: verb + không + result: nghe không hiểu = 聽不懂, exactly as in Mandarin.

s0075.x: cổ = cô ấy, she: a Saigon contraction.

s0088.x: The numbers one to ten. From eleven on they combine: mười một (11), hai mươi (20).

s0089.x: rồi at the end = already: the answer to Em ăn cơm chưa?

s0090.x: Number + giờ = o'clock; the part of the day comes after: chín giờ tối = 晚上九點.

s0091.x: cái này = this (thing), 這個. mắc = expensive in the South.

s0092.x: tiếng + country = its language: tiếng Việt, tiếng Đức, tiếng Anh.

s0093.x: được after the verb = can, manage to, like 會 or 能: nói được tiếng Anh = 會說英文.

s0094.x: lắm after the adjective = very, really. hay = good, interesting, for books, films and songs.

s0095.x: không sao = no problem, 沒關係. đâu at the end makes the denial emphatic and reassuring: 啦.

s0096.x: không before the verb = not, 不.

s0097.x: là + noun = to be. Inside người Đức the order flips against Mandarin: person first, then German.

s0098.x: What describes a noun follows it: giáo viên tiếng Đức = teacher (of) German, 德文老師.

s0099.x: dạy + what + cho + whom = teach something to someone. cho here = to, for; it follows the verb, where Mandarin puts 給 before it.

s0100.x: Possession: the owner follows the noun, ba anh = my dad. của (of) can be added but is usually left out.

s0101.x: The same pattern: má anh = my mom.

s0102.x: verb + được + object = can do it: 會說中文.

s0103.x: mới before the verb = just, recently, 剛.

s0104.x: ở = be at, live in, with no extra verb: 我住在德國.

s0105.x: đâu = where; like all question words it stands where the answer goes.

s0106.x: hả at the end checks what you think you heard: you're in Saigon, right?

s0107.x: làm nghề gì = do which job. Young people also just ask Em làm gì?

s0108.x: sinh viên = university student; a school pupil is học sinh.

s0109.x: ổng = ông ấy, he (an older man). About your own father it sounds casual.

s0110.x: ảnh = anh ấy, he (a young man).

s0111.x: bạn anh = my friend: the owner after the noun again.

s0112.x: The most common reaction: really? thiệt is the Southern form of thật.

s0113.x: vậy = like that: is that so?, 是喔.

s0114.x: trời ơi = oh my god, literally 天啊. ơi calls someone, here heaven.

s0115.x: lại after the verb = again. … được không? = can you…?, 可以…嗎.

s0116.x: thôi opens a goodbye: okay then. đi ngủ = go to sleep.

s0117.x: ngủ ngon = sleep well (ngon = tasty, here: deeply). nghen is a warmer nha.

s0118.x: tiếp after a verb = go on doing it: nói tiếp = 繼續說.

s0119.x: Literally: arrange to meet again, 再見.

s0122.x: The topic first, cái này (this thing), then the question about it. sao at the end = how, 怎麼.

s0123.x: Literally 這個字意思是什麼: the Mandarin order, except that này follows the noun.

s0124.x: sao after the verb = how: viết sao = 怎麼寫, nói sao = 怎麼說.

s0125.x: Literally: you say it like that, that is how? = what do you mean?

s0126.x: Two additions after the verb: lại (again) and chậm chút (a bit slower). … được hông? = can you…?

s0127.x: verb + hông + kịp = not manage to keep up, 跟不上. The same frame as nghe không hiểu.

s0128.x: ủa at the start shows surprise, hả at the end checks.

s0129.x: chưa before the verb = not yet.

s0130.x: sao vậy = what's the matter, 怎麼了. Like 怎麼, sao covers how, why and what's wrong.

s0131.x: ha at the end invites agreement: 對吧、耶.

s0132.x: The judgement comes after the verb phrase: nói tiếng Anh giỏi = 英文說得好.

s0133.x: lắm luôn = really, totally: a stronger lắm.

s0134.x: luôn after a negative = at all: không biết luôn = 完全不知道.

s0135.x: á at the end tells: I'm telling you, 喔、耶.

s0136.x: đi at the end turns it into an invitation, 吧.

s0137.x: The first đi is go, the second the invitation: 你去睡吧.

s0138.x: vậy đi = let's do it like that, 就這樣吧.

s0139.x: hông as the question word, then the person you ask. It really asks whether it is true.

s0140.x: dữ vậy = that intense, that much: 這麼誇張、這麼厲害.

s0141.x: ờ ha = oh right. quên rồi = forgot, 忘了.

s0142.x: gửi + person = send to someone. nè when you hand something over: here you go.

s0143.x: nhắn cho + person = text someone, 傳訊息給….

s0144.x: mới before the verb here = only then, 才, as in 我現在才知道.

s0145.x: gửi + thing + cho + person: send something to someone.

s0146.x: mình = we, you and I. A suggestion as a question: shall we…?

s0147.x: đang before the verb = in the middle of, 在、正在.

s0148.x: The result follows the verb: viết sai = 寫錯.

s0149.x: verb + giùm + person = do it for someone: sửa giùm anh = 幫我改.

s0150.x: nhiều after the thanks = a lot.

s0151.x: có … đâu = there is no … at all: đâu turns it into a denial, 沒什麼啦. Without đâu, Có gì? is a real question.

s0152.x: An adjective as the predicate again: no 是 needed.

s0153.x: nhưng mà = but; vui = fun, happy.
